title: Organophosphate / carbamate poisoning
population: Adults and children (one pathway; ADULT / CHILD lines where doses differ)

items.t: Exposure: pesticide / stock remedy, ingested, skin or inhaled
Muscarinic: salivation, lacrimation, sweating, urination, vomiting, diarrhoea, bronchorrhoea, bronchospasm, bradycardia, hypotension, miosis
Nicotinic: fasciculations, muscle weakness, tachycardia, hypertension, mydriasis
HR and pupils depend on whether muscarinic or nicotinic effects predominate. Low pseudocholinesterase supports the diagnosis — do not wait for it.

decision.t: 10. Diagnosis = SEVERE OP poisoning → atropinise, then REFER (ICU). Adult: refer if ventilatory support is needed; child: all severe cases to ICU
11. ADMIT — atropinise, infuse, watch for intermediate syndrome — stabilise, then continue on the 0 h – Day 5 inpatient chart and the 24-hour nursing record

chart.phase_note: Infusion and weaning start when criteria are met, not on the clock

standing.t: Bolus phase: reassess 3–5 min after every atropine dose (doctor at bedside) — chest secretions, skin, HR, BP, pupils
On infusion: hourly while on infusion and for 24 h after it stops, then 4-hourly — HR, BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature, pupils, chest secretions, axillary sweat, GCS, neck flexion
Extra check 15 min after every rate change
Atropine overdose check at the same times: agitation, fever, bowel sounds, urinary retention
HGT on arrival, 6-hourly while nil by mouth, and with any seizure or drop in LOC

rows.label: 0 h
rows.lead: PPE first. Check the referral / EMS note for atropine (mg) and charcoal already given — do not repeat charcoal. Call Poisons Helpline 0861 555 777 or UFS 082 491 0160 (24 h).

feed.t: Airway, O₂, suction secretions frequently
GCS < 8: protect airway → REFER
Hypoxia, hypercarbia, weak effort: intubate + ventilate → REFER
RSI: avoid suxamethonium (child: also mivacurium) — prolonged paralysis
Decontaminate only once resuscitated: remove clothes, wash body with soap and water, clothes in closed bags
Eyes: irrigate 15–20 min
IV access · hypotension: bolus per shock protocol
Nil by mouth until alert, secretions controlled

tests.t: Pseudocholinesterase — confirmation only, do not wait
If rat poison / unknown pesticide: INR now and at 48 h
If female of child-bearing age: urine βhCG
Record time of ingestion on request forms

treatment.h: Atropine STEP 1 — bronchorrhoea, bronchospasm or bradycardia

treatment.t: ADULT: atropine 2 mg IV bolus; double every 3–5 min until atropinised: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 mg…
ADULT: check ampoule strength (100 mg/10 mL at some sites)
CHILD: atropine 0.05 mg/kg IV over 1 min; double every 3–5 min, e.g. 10 kg: 0.5 → 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 mg (no maximum)
Atropinised = reduced bronchial secretions, dry skin, HR and BP rising, pupils dilating (may be delayed). No response: double. Some response: same or reduced dose
Tachycardia and dilated pupils do not contraindicate atropine in resuscitation
ADULT agitation: diazepam 5–10 mg IV, repeat after 30–60 min if needed
ADULT seizures: lorazepam 4 mg IV, or midazolam 10 mg IV/IM/buccal, or diazepam 10 mg IV; repeat once at 5 min
ADULT: no phenytoin (toxin) — still seizing: REFER
CHILD agitation or seizures: lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg), or midazolam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg) / 0.5 mg/kg buccal, or diazepam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg); repeat once at 5 min
CHILD: then phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV over 5 min (max 600 mg). No phenytoin. REFER
Activated charcoal once stabilised and airway protected — doses in Doses tab
Notify NMC (pesticide poisoning is notifiable)

feed.t: Infusion 10–20% of the STEP 1 total bolus dose per hour
Adult: start at 10%, titrate up to 20% — 40 mg (1 mg/mL) + 160 mL diluent = 0.2 mg/mL; e.g. total 62 mg → 6 mg/h = 30 mL/h
Child: 0.01 mg/mL — remove 1 mL from 100 mL NaCl 0.9%, add 1 mL atropine 1 mg/mL

treatment.t: Activated charcoal now if stable and airway protected
Decontaminate if not yet done
Start the 24-hour nursing record

feed.t: Secretions, bronchospasm or bradycardia recur → increase
Controlled + overdose signs (tachycardia, mydriasis, agitation, pyrexia, reduced bowel sounds, urinary retention) → decrease
No recurrence, no overdose → reduce slowly

treatment.t: Adult: boluses again from 2 mg, doubling; new rate = 0.1 × (STEP 1 + STEP 3 bolus totals), titrate up to 20%
Child: increase the infusion

treatment.t: Adult agitation: diazepam 5–10 mg IV, repeat after 30–60 min if needed
Watch for aspiration

feed.t: No recurrence and no overdose → wean
Do not stop abruptly — wean over at least 24 h
Recurrence on weaning: back to the last effective rate, STEP 3 if needed

treatment.h: Intermediate syndrome watch (1–4 days after the cholinergic crisis)

treatment.t: Neck flexors, bulbar (swallow, cough), respiratory muscles, proximal limbs, cranial nerves

feed.t: Infusion off when weaned. Oral diet

Child: social worker if supervision or neglect concern

items.t: 1 mg/mL ampoule: undiluted — 2 mg = 2 mL · 4 = 4 · 8 = 8 · 16 = 16 mL
100 mg/10 mL: 1 mL + 9 mL diluent = 1 mg/mL
100 mg/10 mL: 200 mg (20 mL) + 180 mL = 1 mg/mL
Rate = 10% of total bolus/h, up to 20%
Bolus 0.05 mg/kg IV over 1 min, doubling
Infusion 10–20% of total bolus dose per hour
0.01 mg/mL: 1 mL removed from 100 mL NaCl 0.9% + atropine 1 mg/mL 1 mL; or 1 mL removed from 50 mL bag + atropine 500 mcg/mL 1 mL
Glycopyrrolate 0.025 mg/kg IV: central atropine toxicity with ongoing peripheral secretions only

items.h: Activated charcoal — once stabilised, airway protected; best within 1 h; not for petroleum solvents

items.t: Child < 6 y: 1 g/kg in 50–100 mL water
Child > 6 y: 20–50 g in 100–300 mL water

items.h: Seizures — benzodiazepine, repeat once at 5 min; never phenytoin in toxin-induced seizures

items.t: Adult: lorazepam 4 mg IV · or midazolam 10 mg IV/IM/buccal · or diazepam 10 mg IV. Not controlled: REFER (refractory)
Child (< 13 y): lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4) · or midazolam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10) / 0.5 mg/kg buccal · or diazepam 0.25 mg/kg IV (max 10)
Child: then phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV (max 600 mg). REFER
Adult: diazepam 5–10 mg IV, repeat after 30–60 min
Tachycardia, mydriasis, agitation, pyrexia, reduced bowel sounds, urinary retention
GCS < 8 · hypoxia, hypercarbia or weak respiratory effort

discharge.title: Discharge criteria — all must be met (conditional items where they apply)

items.t: Off atropine ≥ 24 h, no cholinergic signs
No neck, bulbar or respiratory weakness through the intermediate-syndrome window
If rat poison: INR at 48 h reviewed
Intentional: mental health assessment and plan
Child: safe storage counselling; social worker if concern
Review at 1 week; mental health follow-up if intentional
Return immediately if weakness, trouble breathing or swallowing, drooling, sweating or confusion

nursing.title: 24-hour nursing record — atropine response, overdose and neuro
nursing.period: One sheet per 24 hours; hourly rows while on infusion and for 24 h after it stops (†), then 4-hourly (†)

items.t: Hourly while on infusion and for 24 h after it stops, then 4-hourly; extra check 15 min after every rate change
Chest secretions: wet crackles / drooling Y or N
Axillae: wet or dry · HR · BP · pupils in mm
Same times: temperature, agitation, bowel sounds, bladder / urine passed
Record the rate in mg/h every hour; boluses in Notes
Never stop the infusion abruptly — wean over at least 24 h
RR, SpO₂, GCS at the same times
Neck flexion: lift head off pillow — N (normal) or W (weak); note swallow and cough
HGT on arrival, 6-hourly while nil by mouth, and with any seizure or drop in LOC

call.t: Overdose signs (tachycardia, dilated pupils, agitation, fever, absent bowel sounds, urinary retention)
RR, SpO₂ or breathing effort worse than the patient's baseline
New neck, swallowing or breathing weakness
